Implement the beat clock module (`src/utils/beat.ts`)

## Summary
Create a new pure, unit-testable beat clock module that derives a beat period from a configurable BPM (default 80 BPM → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes quantisation helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — Module at `src/utils/beat.ts` exposes `beatPeriodMs` (derived from configurable BPM, default 80), `nextTick(elapsedTime, interval)`, and `shotTimeFor(currentTime, interval)` helpers.
- [ ] **AC2** — All helpers are pure and deterministic given an input time — no `Date` or frame coupling.
- [ ] **AC3** — The beat anchor is configurable (defaults to 0/scene start) and advances with game time (pauses with the game).
- [ ] **AC4** — Unit tests cover: period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override changing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert that `nextTick(t, interval)` returns the smallest multiple of `interval` at/after `t`, and `shotTimeFor` snaps to the correct grid tick.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC1** — [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.

## Constraints
- No audio or visual beat indicators — silent internal scheduling only.
- Must work with Phasers delta-time model (ms-based).
- Default BPM: 80 (beat period: 750 ms). All per-weapon intervals are exact subdivisions.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure beat clock module.
- `src/utils/beat.test.ts` — **NEW** — unit tests.

## Risks
- Minimal: the module is pure and self-contained. Edge cases: large dt values (frame drops), zero elapsed time.
data.title: Implement pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock module

# Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview

## Context

The runtime auto-sequencer (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is fully implemented but not wired into the game. There is no way for designers or testers to interact with it visually. This work item creates a gym scene that provides a hands-on interface for designing and previewing difficulty curves.

discovered-from:AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X

## Goal

Add a new **Dev Utilities** category/section to the gym index, and create a gym scene within it that provides:

1. **Curve editor** — an interactive way to define the target difficulty curve (array of scores, one per wave)
2. **Regenerate button** — when clicked, runs the sequencer against the current curve and displays the resulting waves
3. **Wave list** — shows each generated wave with its enemy composition, target difficulty, and the resulting wave
4. **Edit-to-clear behaviour** — if the curve is edited, the wave list is cleared and replaced with an instruction to click the regenerate button

## Scope

- Add a **Dev Utilities** column/section to the gym index (GymIndex.ts) — follows the same pattern as the existing ENEMIES and Bosses columns
- Create src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts (and its test file)
- The scene uses the existing sequencer() from difficultySequencer.ts
- Plain-DOM tuning panel overlay (same pattern as GymPlayer) for the curve editor
- Phaser canvas for the wave list display (Phaser text objects)

## Curve editor design

- Each wave in the curve is represented as a row with:
  - A numeric slider (0–100) for the target difficulty
  - A Remove button to delete that wave row
- An "Add Wave" button to append a new wave row at the end
- The "Regenerate" button runs the sequencer and populates the wave list below
- When the curve is edited (any slider moved, wave added/removed), the wave list is cleared and replaced with instruction text: "Edit made — click Regenerate to preview"

## Wave list display

- Each wave entry shows:
  - Wave number
  - Target difficulty
  - Enemy composition (enemy type, count)
  - Whether shooting is enabled
- Entries rendered as Phaser text objects, ordered top-to-bottom

## Non-goals

- Saving/loading curves (could be added later)
- Visual preview of enemy formations (text-only for now)
- Drag-to-reorder waves in the curve editor

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Gym index shows a "Dev Utilities" section** — a new column or section in the gym index listing gym scenes under the Dev Utilities category
2. **GymCurveSequencer scene is listed** under the Dev Utilities section and can be launched from the gym index
3. **Curve editor works** — user can add wave rows, remove wave rows, and adjust target difficulty via sliders (0–100)
4. **Regenerate button** — clicking it runs sequencer() with the current curve and candidate pool, populating the wave list
5. **Wave list is cleared on curve edit** — when the user edits the curve (any change), the wave list is replaced with instruction text to click regenerate
6. **Wave entries display correctly** — each shows wave number, target difficulty, enemy composition, and shooting status
7. **Back to index button** works (arrow-left INDEX)
8. **ESC returns to main menu** (consistent with other gym scenes)
9. **All tests pass** — the scene has unit tests verifying the curve editor and regenerate flow

## Revision — audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the first implementation with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. Make the wave description a table, with column headings. Provide a help box in the bottom right summarizing each column.

Additional acceptance criteria:

10. **Wave preview is a table** — the wave preview renders a table with column headings (Wave, Target, Composition, Shooting) and one aligned row per wave.
11. **Column guide help box** — a help box anchored to the bottom-right of the canvas summarises each wave-table column.

## Revision — second audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the implementation again with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. The UI works, but the generated levels are not good. Firstly, why do we have an actual and error value? Why don't we just create as close the target as possible? Secondly, the higher levels seem to just repeat the phaser with shooting.

Root cause confirmed by reproducing the sequencer output: `sequencer()` picked exactly one candidate group per wave and a single group's `enemyDifficulty` score saturates around 33 (e.g. `phaser×12`), so every target at or above ~40 produced the identical `phaser×12` wave — hence the large error values and the repetition.

Revised acceptance criteria:

12. **Wave generation reaches the target** — the preview table no longer shows redundant ACTUAL/ERROR columns; the table columns are WAVE / TARGET / COMPOSITION / SHOOTING. The sequencer composes a wave from one or more candidate groups so the wave's summed difficulty is within a small tolerance of the target for every target above the old single-group ceiling (previously capped at ~33) up to 100.
13. **Higher waves are varied** — waves with different (especially higher) targets produce meaningfully different enemy compositions instead of every high wave repeating the same archetype (e.g. `phaser` with shooting).

## Key Files

- src/scenes/GymIndex.ts — add Dev Utilities section
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts — new scene
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.test.ts — tests for the scene
- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts — sequencer (extended to compose multi-group waves)
- src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts — existing scorer (read-only)
- src/core/enemyConfig.ts — existing enemy configs for candidate pool
- src/utils/gymNavigation.ts — shared back-to-index navigation
- src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts — gym scene auto-discovery (no changes needed, scene auto-appears)
data.title: Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview

# Goal

Fix the audit runner's parent-first flow so that child `partial` verdicts caused by unserviced in-main-slot items are treated as "not assessed" rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision, and add diagnostic clarity.

# Background

In `--child-in-main-slot` mode (default), child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking agent session. In non-interactive runs (e.g. downtime workers), these items are never serviced, leaving all child AC verdicts as `partial`.

Currently, `_build_issue_json` treats ALL `partial` verdicts as unacceptable, causing the parent to report "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met, because the child partials (from unserviced in-main-slot work) are counted as failures.

# Implementation Plan

## 1. Track in-main-slot partial verdicts

Add a `verdict_reason` field to child AC results when they are `partial` due to in-main-slot unserviced work. The `_phase1_review_child_acs` and `_deep_analyze_child` functions already set `verdict: "partial"` with evidence like `"pending (main-session review)"` in in-main-slot mode. We need to mark these explicitly with `verdict_reason: "unserviced-in-main-slot"`.

## 2. Handle partials in `_build_issue_json`

Modify `all_ac_acceptable` computation to skip child ACs whose `partial` verdict has `verdict_reason == "unserviced-in-main-slot"`. These should be treated as "not assessed" and NOT block the parent's readiness-to-close decision.

## 3. Add diagnostic output

In the audit summary/JSON output, surface a clear diagnostic that distinguishes:
- Children with `partial` verdicts from unserviced in-main-slot work → "not assessed"
- Children with genuine `partial` or `unmet` verdicts → "not-ready"

Add a `children_assessment` section to the `_build_issue_json` output listing `unserviced_in_main_slot` child IDs and `genuine_not_ready` child IDs.

# Acceptance Criteria
- AC2: Parent audit treats in-main-slot unserviced partials as "not assessed" (does NOT block ready-to-close)
- AC3: Audit output includes diagnostic distinguishing unserviced-in-main-slot partials from genuine failures

# Constraints
- Must not change behaviour of interactive runs (where agent CAN service in-main-slot items)
- Must be backward-compatible with persisted audit results

# Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase1_review_child_acs`, `_deep_analyze_child`, `_build_issue_json`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — existing in-main-slot tests
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — freshness tests (verify no regression)
data.title: Fix in-main-slot partial verdict handling and diagnostics (AC2-AC3)

# Test: gyms drop minerals on kill

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic gym tests that fail while the gyms do not drop minerals, pinning the behaviour the gym-wiring task must deliver.

## Required coverage

- Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row (via the shared destruction path and via the EXPLODE button) increases the live mineral count by exactly one at the asteroid's position.
- A large/medium asteroid splits into its children without a direct mineral drop.
- No double drop: a single destruction produces exactly one drop (not one per path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the gym drop behaviour; `npm test` for the gym suites passes.
- Tests assert the drop position and count, not merely that the count increased, and are deterministic (seeded RNG).
- Tests fail before the gym-wiring task lands and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`

# Intake Brief — When ships explode when a level times out we need major SFX explosion (AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC)

## Headline

Add a new dedicated, layered "major explosion" SFX to the wave-timeout path,
played once per detonating ship (with a concurrency/rate limiter), so the 10×
detonation of surviving enemies is no longer silent.

## Problem statement

When a wave times out, every surviving non-asteroid enemy detonates at 10×
scale (`WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE`), but no explosion sound plays for those
detonations. The only audio on the timeout path is the generic player
life-loss cue (`playDestructionSound()` via `_loseLife(false)`), so the
dramatic 10× visual blast lands silently and the moment reads as flat.

## Users

- **Player** — the wave-timeout wipe should be audible as a major explosion,
  making the lost life and the 10× detonation feel consequential.
- **Developer / designer tuning feel** — one place (exported constants) to tune
  the cue's layering, volume, duration and voice cap.

### Example user story

- As a **player**, when the level timer hits zero and my remaining enemies
  detonate, I hear a large, heavy explosion cue so the moment reads as a major
  event rather than a silent animation.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_timeoutWave()` detonates every non-asteroid
  survivor via `s.entity.destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)` and calls
  `_loseLife(false)`; it plays **no SFX for the detonations**.
  `WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE = 10`.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `destroySelf(scale)` → `playExplosion(scale)`
  only spawns particles; the class comment states audio is played by the scene
  at destruction time.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playDestructionSound()` (generic 440→60 Hz
  sawtooth pop) and the layered `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (impact thump +
  descending body + noise tail). No "major" or timeout-specific cue exists.
- GDD §7.3 documents the two existing cues and states "the wave-timeout life
  penalty and shield absorption keep the generic cue". It also flags the risk
  "SFX rate limiting — … avoid stacking more than 3–4 concurrent SFX
  instances".
- Tests live in `src/audio/effects.test.ts`, `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts`
  and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Add a new dedicated, layered `playMajorExplosionSound()` cue in
`src/audio/effects.ts` and wire it into `PlayScene._timeoutWave()` so it fires
once per detonating ship, guarded by a concurrency/rate limiter so stacked cues
stay within the GDD §7.3 audio ceiling. Document the new cue in GDD §7.3 and
cover it with automated tests.

## Producer decisions (recorded)

- **Q1 — Blast granularity: B** → one heavy cue **per detonating ship**, with
  attenuation/rate-limiting.
- **Q2 — Cue identity: A** → a **new dedicated** `playMajorExplosionSound()`,
  not a reuse of `playPlayerDestructionSound()`.
- **Q3 — Player life-loss cue on timeout: A** → keep the **generic**
  `playDestructionSound()` for the player's timeout life loss; only the enemy
  detonations get the major blast cue.

## Assumptions

1. The limiter caps concurrent major-explosion voices at an exported
   `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` (default aligned to the GDD's "≤ 3–4 concurrent
   SFX" guidance); triggers beyond the cap are coalesced/attenuated rather than
   stacking at full gain. [ASSUMPTION]
2. Scope is audio only — the 10× particle blast already exists, so no new VFX.
   [ASSUMPTION]
3. `PlayScene` is the only wave-timeout path (no gym scene has a wave timeout),
   so wiring is confined to `PlayScene._timeoutWave()`. [ASSUMPTION]
4. The cue routes through the existing SFX master gain/mute plumbing and is a
   safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests, autoplay-blocked
   browsers). [ASSUMPTION]

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new dedicated `playMajorExplosionSound()` is defined in
   `src/audio/effects.ts` using layered procedural synthesis (impact thump +
   descending body + noise tail), with every amplitude, duration and voice-cap
   value exposed as an exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constant; the cue is
   documented in GDD §7.3.
2. When a wave/level times out with surviving non-asteroid enemies, the major
   explosion cue is triggered **once per detonating ship** (verified by a
   `PlayScene` test whose spy count equals the number of detonated survivors).
3. A concurrency/rate limiter keeps stacked per-ship cues within the GDD §7.3
   audio ceiling: no more than `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` concurrent
   major-explosion voices, with excess triggers attenuated/coalesced — verified
   by unit tests that exercise many simultaneous triggers.
4. When a wave/level times out with no enemies remaining, no major-explosion
   cue plays and the player's generic life-loss cue is unchanged (no
   `playPlayerDestructionSound()` on this path) — verified by tests.
5. The cue routes through the SFX master volume/mute and is a safe no-op
   without an `AudioContext` — verified by tests.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- All SFX remain **procedural** (Web Audio API, zero external audio assets) per
  GDD §7.3.
- Respect the GDD §7.3 ceiling and the "avoid stacking more than 3–4 concurrent
  SFX instances" risk mitigation.
- No new gameplay behaviour: the timeout detonation/one-life penalty is
  unchanged; this is feedback only.
- No new VFX.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playMajorExplosionSound()` and its
  `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` tuning/limiter constants (mirroring the layered
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()` structure).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Call the new cue once per detonating ship in
  `_timeoutWave()` (alongside `destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)`);
  leave `_loseLife(false)` and its generic cue untouched.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` / `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` — Unit tests
  for layering, limiter/voice cap, master volume/mute routing and
  no-AudioContext no-op.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — Timeout wiring tests (one cue per ship, none
  when no enemies, generic player cue unchanged).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 SFX event catalog and player audio
  character section: document the new major-explosion cue and its limiter.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Limiter tuning may need an audio playtest.** Whether the per-ship stack
  reads as one "major" blast or as mud cannot be judged from unit tests alone;
  `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` and per-voice gain are exported for tuning.
  [Medium]
- **Masking/clipping risk.** Many near-simultaneous heavy cues could mask
  other SFX or clip; mitigated by the voice cap/attenuation (GDD §7.3 "avoid
  stacking more than 3–4 concurrent SFX instances"). [Medium]
- **Browser autoplay policy.** The cue stays silent until a user gesture
  starts the `AudioContext`; it must remain a safe no-op when no context
  exists. [Low]
- **Scope-creep guard.** Reusing the new major cue for other events (boss
  death, P4 bomb clear, player death) is out of scope; record those as linked
  work items rather than widening this item. [Low]
- **Assumption:** no gym wave-timeout path exists today; if one is added
  later, it must reuse the same cue + limiter rather than duplicating it.
  [Low]

## Related work

- AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x
  scale and cost a life (added the timeout detonation; completed).
- AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L — Asteroids should not explode when time runs out,
  instead carry them over (completed).
- AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY — Need juice when the player is destroyed (precedent for
  a dedicated layered cue; completed).
- AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A — dedicated player-destruction cue (implemented
  `playPlayerDestructionSound`).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V — Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player
  deaths (completed).
- AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH — Add randomness to explosion (completed).
- AH-0MUA8B6MT006M1KS — SFX master volume + mute plumbing in effects.ts
  (completed).
- AH-0MUA8BEUR006RWCI — SettingsScene: SFX volume slider + mute toggle
  (completed).
- AH-0MU3VPIA900697E8 — Ensure all enemies have SFX on their fire event
  (completed).
- AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1 — Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD
  (completed).

## Related work (automated report)

> Generated by the `find-related` skill. Conservative ranking; treat as
> suggestions, not a complete list.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUBYXR280018HST** – PlayScene: wire absorb animation + pop SFX into collection path (completed)
- **AH-0MTFU1GAO009KDBM** – [test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52** – Extract common enemy base class for regular enemies (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: absorption, ac3, acceptance, add, added (+200 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absorption, ac3, add, added, also (+199 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, added, already, also, animation (+160 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Blast granularity: Should the "major SFX explosion" be one cue per
  timeout event, or one cue per detonating ship?** — Answer (producer, via
  interactive reply): **B) one heavy cue per detonating ship, with
  attenuation/rate-limiting.** Agent recommendation had been A (single cue);
  producer chose B, so a limiter is now an explicit AC. Final accepted answer:
  B.
- **Q2 — Cue identity: Should this be a new dedicated cue or a reuse of an
  existing one?** — Answer (producer, via interactive reply): **A) a new
  dedicated `playMajorExplosionSound()`.** Final accepted answer: A.
- **Q3 — Player life-loss cue on timeout: upgrade to the heavy
  player-destruction cue, or only the enemy detonations?** — Answer (producer,
  via interactive reply): **A) keep the generic player life-loss cue and add
  only the blast cue.** Final accepted answer: A.
data.title: When ships explode when a level times out we need major SFX explosion

## Goal
As a developer, I want a documented, repeatable reproduction and root-cause analysis for the flaky `isTransitioning()` assertion, so the fix targets the real source and does not mask a production defect.

## Context
Parent: AH-0MUHA0MMP001DZ5C (Flaky PlayScene wave-transition test). Three recorded occurrences across different PlayScene transition tests (AC5 line 443, AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 AC4 line 665, AH-0MU7JTF9W008B8HW AC4 line 594) all fail as `expect(scene.isTransitioning()).toBe(false -> true)` right after `killAllEnemies`. Leading hypotheses: **H1** — the live Phaser requestAnimationFrame loop advances the scene an unpredictable amount (during/after the fixed 150 ms `bootDelay`), draining the 1.5 s `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` timer before the assertion under parallel load; **H2** — `killAllEnemies` only checks `getAliveCount() === 0`, so a kill path that does not drive `_advanceAfterKill()`/`_startTransition()` leaves `isTransitioning()` false; **H3** — a genuine `WaveManager` `_enemiesAlive` register/unregister desync or transition-timer ordering defect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified and documented: the flakiness source is demonstrated with evidence (a failing reproduction under parallel load plus the code path that produces the nondeterministic state), and recorded in a comment on the parent item.
- [ ] The analysis explicitly distinguishes test-harness nondeterminism from any production accounting/ordering bug in `PlayScene`/`WaveManager`.
- [ ] Each of H1, H2 and H3 is confirmed or eliminated with concrete evidence (code path, captured state dump, or reproduction log), not assumption.
- [ ] If the flake is not reproducible, a state-dump diagnostic and code-path analysis are recorded and the reason it cannot be reproduced is documented.


## Minimal Implementation
- Add a temporary diagnostic (log `transitionTimer`, `waveManager.enemiesAlive`, `getAliveCount()` around the failing assertion) or a state-dump hook.
- Run the focused `PlayScene.test.ts` transition tests repeatedly under parallel CPU load and capture a failure, or prove a bounded non-reproduction.
- Trace the code path from the final enemy kill to `_startTransition()` and from the real Phaser loop's `update()` -> `tick(dt)` to `_onTransitionComplete()`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`

## Deliverables
- Root-cause comment on AH-0MUHA0MMP001DZ5C distinguishing H1/H2/H3.
- Reproduction command/script and captured evidence.

# Intake brief — Game over screen should have focus on the initials input field

**Headline:** On game over the initials field should be the active, visibly highlighted control so the player can type immediately, rather than the "Return to Menu" button. Investigation shows the functional focus model already targets the initials field (unit and full-transition tests pass), so the producer must confirm whether the observed defect is a real functional failure in the browser or a misleading visual affordance.

**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** medium

> **Original request (preserved):** "when the game over screen is displayed the focus is on return to menu, it should be on the initials input field"

## Problem statement

When the game-over screen (`GameOverScene`) opens for a qualifying score, the player should be able to type their initials straight away. The report says the on-screen focus sits on **Return to Menu** instead, so the initials field does not look (or, in some environment, does not behave) as the active control.

## Users

- **As an arcade player who has just finished a qualifying run**, when the game-over screen appears I want the initials field to be focused and clearly highlighted, so I can type my three letters immediately without pressing Tab or clicking.

  > **User story:** As a player, when I have earned a high score I want my first A–Z key press to enter the first initial, so entering my name is one uninterrupted action.

## Investigation findings (verified against HEAD `e23b43a` on `dev`)

- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` `create()` registers the initials field with the shared `FocusManager` **before** the Return to Menu button, so index 0 (the initials field) receives default focus and the visible focus style.
- The dedicated suites pass: `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` (AC1 asserts `getFocusedIndex() === 0` and a non-empty focus stroke) and `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts`.
- The **full real-transition path** is already covered by `src/scenes/SceneNavigation.test.ts` (`AC1+AC2+AC3 — the full loop is drivable by keyboard`): after `PlayScene` → `GameOverScene`, typing `a`/`b`/`c` yields `ABC` with no Tab/click, and that suite passes.
- The GDD documents the intended behaviour: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.1, §4.5 and the *Keyboard entry (game-over screen)* section state the initials field is focused by default.
- `main` and `dev` both contain this behaviour (`259ee8e AH-0MUBZTPDR003A1JT: GameOverScene keyboard support`), so it is not a stale-branch difference.
- The automated harness stubs the canvas and emits Phaser key events directly, so it does **not** exercise a real browser's DOM keyboard focus or the actual rendered focus highlight.

**Conclusion:** the functional "which control is focused" requirement is already implemented and tested. The reported symptom is most plausibly (a) a real-browser keyboard-focus failure not exercised by the jsdom harness, or (b) a visual-affordance problem: the button's persistent dark background box reads as the selected control while the initials field only shows a thin white text outline over three underscores.

## Desired change

Make the initials field the unambiguous active control on the game-over screen. Depending on the producer's answer (see Open questions), this is either:

- **(a) functional** — fix the real-browser path so the first key press after the screen opens edits the initials; or
- **(b) visual** — give the focused initials field a clear, boxed focus indicator clearly distinguishable from the unfocused Return to Menu button (and from the highlighted prospective leaderboard row).

## Acceptance Criteria (proposed — pending producer answer)

- **AC1 — Focus is on the initials field.** When `GameOverScene` opens for a qualifying score, the initials entry field is the focused control (focus index 0) and the Return to Menu button is not focused; verified by `GameOverScene`/`SceneNavigation` tests.
- **AC2 — Immediate typing.** The first A–Z key press after the screen opens appends to the initials and Backspace deletes, with no Tab or click required, verified both in the automated suite and manually in a real browser (`npm run dev`).
- **AC3 — Unambiguous visible focus.** The focused initials field shows a clearly visible focus highlight that a player can distinguish at a glance from the unfocused Return to Menu button; the highlight is documented in the GDD focus-model description.
- **AC4 — Reported state reproduced first (TDD).** Before any fix, a failing regression test (or a documented, evidence-backed real-browser reproduction) captures the operator-reported state; the fix makes it pass. If the functional focus is confirmed already correct, the regression test pins the focus/affordance contract so it cannot regress.
- **AC5 — No regression to existing keyboard/pointer behaviour.** Tab/Shift+Tab/arrow cycling, Enter auto-submit, Enter/Space on the button, and pointer click on Return to Menu all continue to work (existing `GameOverScene`, `SceneNavigation` and `focusManager` suites stay green).
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (in particular `docs/Game Design Document.md` keyboard-entry sections).
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Use the shared `FocusManager` (`src/utils/focusManager.ts`) — do not add a scene-local focus mechanism.
- Preserve the public/test seams and existing pointer/keyboard behaviour; changes should be surgical.
- Match existing Phaser style (uses `strokeThickness`, not `strokeWidth`).
- UK English in all written output.
- Implementation only proceeds through `/skill:implement`; this item does not authorise code changes.

## Existing state

- Game over screen: `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` (initials entry + full leaderboard + live prospective row).
- Shared focus model: `src/utils/focusManager.ts`; `GameOverScene` routes text keys itself and delegates focus keys to the manager.
- Full-loop coverage: `src/scenes/SceneNavigation.test.ts`; focused-field coverage: `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.1 *Menu & UI navigation*, §4.5 and §5 *Keyboard entry (game-over screen)*; `README.md` controls section.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — focus registration order and/or the visible focus affordance on the initials field.
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` — regression test pinning default focus and immediate typing.
- `src/scenes/SceneNavigation.test.ts` — full `PlayScene` → `GameOverScene` keyboard path.
- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` — only if a shared focus defect is found (affects every menu).
- `src/ui/leaderboardView.ts` — only if the prospective-row highlight contributes to the ambiguous focus display.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.1/§4.5/§5 and `README.md` — documentation sync.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUBZTPDR003A1JT` — **GameOverScene keyboard support** (completed): introduced the focus model on this screen; its AC1 is exactly "initials field is focused by default" — this item is effectively a regression/report against that AC.
- `AH-0MUE86S5F002VVQD` — **Leaderboard entry screen should show position in table** (completed): most recent `GameOverScene` change (live prospective row + highlight).
- `AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9` — **Keyboard only control** (completed): parent epic that defines the shared in-canvas focus model.
- `AH-0MU731426003FE71` — **Implement GameOverScene — scoring, lives, game-over flow** (completed).
- `AH-0MUJRJ3IK006OPGD` / `AH-0MUJQ7G5C005Y8T9` — **When entering initials allow upper and lower case** (open): same input field; check for overlap when implementing.

## Open questions (blocking intake completion)

1. **What exactly did the operator observe?** The functional focus model already targets the initials field and all automated tests (including the full `PlayScene` → `GameOverScene` keyboard loop) pass. Did typing letters fail to enter initials in a real browser, or was the concern that the button *looked* focused?
   **Recommended:** Provide the exact reproduction (browser, build/branch, steps, and whether letters typed into the field) or a screenshot — this determines whether the fix is functional (a) or a visible-affordance change (b).

2. **If the functional focus is already correct, is improving the visible focus affordance in scope?** The Return to Menu button keeps a persistent dark background box, while the initials field only gets a thin white text outline on three underscores.
   **Recommended:** Yes — give the focused initials field a clearly boxed highlight so it is obviously the active control, and lock the functional focus with a regression test.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What exactly did the operator observe — a functional failure to type initials in a real browser, or a visual impression that Return to Menu is focused?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (no producer available in-session; awaiting producer response). Context: `GameOverScene.test.ts` and `SceneNavigation.test.ts` both pass and assert initials-first focus and immediate typing via the Phaser keyboard plugin.
- Q2: "Is improving the visible focus affordance on the initials field in scope if the functional focus is already correct?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer response). Context: `FocusManager` gives the focused control a brighter colour plus a white text stroke; the initials field is only three underscores, whereas the button has a persistent dark background.
- Research (self-directed, repo search): "Is the reported behaviour reproducible from the current source?" — Inspected `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`, `src/utils/focusManager.ts`, `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/SceneNavigation.test.ts`, `src/core/Leaderboard.ts`, `src/core/gameConfig.ts`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, and the git history of `GameOverScene.ts`/`focusManager.ts` on `dev` and `main`. Result: the initials field is registered first and receives default focus; unit and full-transition suites pass; the GDD specifies the same. No source-level regression found, so the discrepancy is unresolved without operator input.

## Summary

Add the pure, engine-agnostic danger-detection helper that decides when the player is "in danger" (parent AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8). Per producer answers Q1 and Q5, danger is the **combined** count of hostile bodies and hostile bullets whose centre lies within `DANGER_RADIUS = 2 × SHIP_SIZE` (40 px) of the ship, and the player is in danger when that count is `>= DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD = 3`. This item is **test-first**: write the failing unit tests before implementing the helper.

## Why

Phase Shift becomes an automatic, reactive defensive tool; it needs a single, correct, unit-testable proximity judgement shared by every combat scene. Without it the auto-trigger has no input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1.1 — `src/core/constants.ts` exports `DANGER_RADIUS` (= `2 * SHIP_SIZE`, i.e. 40 with `SHIP_SIZE = 20`) and `DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD` (= 3); both are used by the helper (no duplicated literals).
- [ ] AC1.2 — A pure helper (e.g. `countThreatsInRange(ship, bodies, bullets)` and `isInDanger(...)`) lives in `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` with **no Phaser import**.
- [ ] AC1.3 — Counting is by **centre-to-centre** distance from the ship; a threat exactly on the radius boundary (distance == `DANGER_RADIUS`) counts as inside.
- [ ] AC1.4 — Boundary tests: exactly 3 combined threats → in danger; 2 → not in danger; a threat just inside the radius counts and one just outside does not.
- [ ] AC1.5 — Enemy bodies (asteroids, boss, boss minions and all enemy archetypes) and live enemy bullets count; player bullets and minerals do **not** count.
- [ ] AC1.6 — `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass; the new tests fail against the pre-change (absent-helper) implementation, demonstrating TDD.
- [ ] AC1.7 — JSDoc on the helper documents the 40 px / >= 3 rule and the producer decision (Q1/Q5).

- [ ] Traceability — parent AC1 (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8): [ ] **AC1 — Danger detection is measurable and correct.** A pure, unit-testable helper counts hostile entities + hostile bullets within `2 × SHIP_SIZE` of the ship and reports "in danger" when the combined count is ≥ 3. Boundary cases are covered: exactly 3 threats triggers; 2 threats do not; threats just inside the radius count and just outside do not; asteroids, boss/minions and all enemy bullet types count; player bullets and minerals do not.


## Minimal Implementation

- Add the two constants to `src/core/constants.ts`.
- Create `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` with a small, total, allocation-light API: `distanceSq`-based counting, accepting read-only `{x,y}` arrays so it is trivially testable and reusable from the scene.
- Add `src/powerups/dangerDetection.test.ts` covering AC1.3–AC1.5.

**Key Files:**
- `src/core/constants.ts`
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts`
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None (foundational). Parent: AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8.

Parent: AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO (bug, high).

## Goal / User story

As a tester, I want deterministic tests that assert a wave completes as soon as
the enemy ships are gone (regardless of live asteroids), and that asteroids and
minerals persist across wave/level transitions, so the new wave rule cannot
silently regress.

This is the **test-first** work item for the parent bug: write/adjust the tests
so they encode the new rule and fail (red) against the current, old-rule code.

## Scope

Update the tests that currently assert the old rule and add new coverage:

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`:
  - Replace `AC6 — the wave clears only after ALL split children are destroyed`.
  - Replace `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5 — carried-over asteroids are re-registered…`.
  - Update the asteroid-integration accounting assertions that expect a split
    child / released asteroid to increment `enemiesAlive` (approx. lines 1232,
    1257).
  - Update the asteroid-spawner integration assertion that a released asteroid
    increments `enemiesAlive` (approx. lines 2327, 2349).
  - Add: wave clears with live asteroids present; `enemiesAlive` excludes
    asteroids and split children; asteroids persist across a wave transition
    and across a level transition; timeout does not re-register asteroids;
    minerals persist across a transition; boss-entry clearing still destroys
    carried-over asteroids.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`: re-frame the "dynamic spawn registration"
  suite as the generic seam (drop the asteroid-semantics claim); keep the API
  tests, because the API is retained.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Wave completion ignores asteroids — test: the wave clears while non-asteroid
  enemy ships are destroyed even when asteroids remain alive, and
  `WaveManager.enemiesAlive` excludes them.
- Minerals persist — test: minerals already on the field remain in place across
  wave and level transitions.
- Boss entry keeps clearing asteroids — test: carried-over asteroids are still
  destroyed when the boss encounter begins.
- Tests updated and comprehensive — unit/integration tests cover wave clearing
  with live asteroids, `enemiesAlive` excluding asteroids and split children,
  persistence across wave and level transitions, and timeout not re-registering
  asteroids.
- A test asserts a released offscreen asteroid and a split child do not
  increment `WaveManager.enemiesAlive`.
- A test asserts surviving asteroids remain alive and continue to move after a
  wave transition and after a level transition.
- A test asserts a surviving asteroid is not re-registered on wave timeout (for
  example, `enemiesAlive` after timeout equals the next wave's enemy-ship
  count).
- All added/updated tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no wall-clock waits)

# Stop registering asteroids with the WaveManager

Parent: AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO (bug, high).

## Goal / User story

As a player, I want a wave to complete as soon as the enemy ships are gone, so
drifting asteroids do not stall my progress. As a developer, I want wave
accounting expressed in one place so it cannot drift between game and tests.

Asteroids must no longer influence `WaveManager.enemiesAlive`; they persist in
the field across wave and level transitions as classic-Asteroids debris.

## Scope note (extra call site)

The parent brief's predicted Key Files list two registration sites
(`_spawnScheduledAsteroid`, `_splitAsteroid`) plus the timeout re-registration.
Repository research found a **fourth** production call site:
`PlayScene.spawnAsteroidAt(x, y, sizeTier)` (public helper used by tests and the
mineral gym) also calls `registerDynamicSpawn(1)`. It is spawned-asteroid
registration and must be removed too, or asteroids placed through it would
still gate the wave.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Wave completion ignores asteroids — when all non-asteroid enemies in the wave
  are destroyed it clears regardless of how many asteroids remain alive, and
  `enemiesAlive` excludes asteroids and split children.
- Asteroids persist — surviving asteroids remain alive in the scene across wave
  and level transitions, with motion, wrapping, rotation and shootability
  unchanged.
- Split behaviour preserved (gameplay only) — destroying a large/medium
  asteroid still spawns exactly two smaller children at its position with
  divergent directions; the split no longer registers a dynamic spawn.
- Wave-timeout unchanged for ships — on wave-timeout every surviving
  non-asteroid enemy still detonates at 10x scale and costs exactly one life;
  surviving asteroids are not re-registered and remain alive and persistent.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- `PlayScene._spawnScheduledAsteroid`, `PlayScene._splitAsteroid` and the public
  `PlayScene.spawnAsteroidAt` no longer call `registerDynamicSpawn`.
- `PlayScene._timeoutWave` no longer re-registers surviving asteroids (the
  `survivingAsteroids` re-registration block is removed).
- No production code path registers asteroids with the `WaveManager`; a grep of
  `src/` (excluding `*.test.ts`) finds no asteroid `registerDynamicSpawn` call
  site.
- `registerDynamicSpawn` / `unregisterDynamicSpawn` remain on `WaveManager`
  (kept as a general dynamic-spawn seam) with a doc comment clarifying that
  asteroids are not registered; `_enemiesAlive` semantics are unchanged.
- Code comments in `PlayScene` (scheduled spawn, split, timeout and
  `spawnAsteroidAt`) state that asteroids are not wave-accounted and persist
  across transitions.
- `_clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry` is unchanged and still destroys carried-over
  asteroids on boss entry.
- The tests from the preceding test-first item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Delete the four `registerDynamicSpawn(...)` calls in `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- Delete the surviving-asteroid re-registration block in `_timeoutWave` and the
  now-unused `survivingAsteroids` local.
- Update the related JSDoc/comments in `PlayScene` and the `WaveManager` doc
  comment for the dynamic-spawn seam.
- Do **not** touch the shared split helper (`src/scenes/core/asteroidSplit.ts`)
  or the gyms.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — remove asteroid dynamic-spawn registration and update comments.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — clarify the dynamic-spawn seam doc comment.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the test-first item (tests must be red first).

## Deliverables

- Asteroid-free wave accounting in `PlayScene`.
- Passing tests from the test-first item plus the existing suite.

## Verification

- `grep -rn registerDynamicSpawn src/ --include=*.ts` shows only `WaveManager`
  and `*.test.ts` references.
- `npm test -- --run` is green.

# Major-explosion cue and constants

## Goal
Add an exported `playMajorExplosionSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts`: a new dedicated, layered "major explosion" cue (impact thump + descending body + filtered-noise tail), distinct from the generic `playDestructionSound()` and the player `playPlayerDestructionSound()`, with every tuning value exposed as an exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constant, plus unit tests.

## User story
As a player, when the level timer hits zero and my remaining enemies detonate, I hear a large, heavy explosion cue so the moment reads as a major event rather than a silent animation.

## Scope
- New exported `playMajorExplosionSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts`, mirroring the layered structure of `playPlayerDestructionSound()`: (1) deep impact thump, (2) descending body sweep, (3) filtered-noise shrapnel tail.
- Every frequency endpoint, duration, layer gain and the voice cap exposed as exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constants (no inline tuning literals in the cue body).
- All layers route through the existing master SFX gain (`ensureMasterGain`) so SFX volume/mute plumbing applies.
- Unit tests in `src/audio/effects.test.ts`; master routing tests in `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts`.
- The voice limiter itself is a separate child (`Major-explosion voice limiter`); this item may export the `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` constant but wires no limiter logic.

## Constraints
- Procedural Web Audio synthesis only; zero external audio assets (GDD §7.3).
- Must never throw when audio is unavailable (mirror the existing safe no-op pattern).
- Must not modify `playDestructionSound()` or `playPlayerDestructionSound()` behaviour.
- Keep layer gains within the documented cue ceiling so the cue does not drown other SFX.

## Key Files
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new cue + `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constants.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — unit tests.
- `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` — master volume/mute routing tests.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC (AC1, AC5); GDD §7.3 Audio Direction.
- Precedent: `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` `blip()` / `ensureMasterGain()` helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `playMajorExplosionSound()` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts` and is a safe no-op that never throws without an `AudioContext`.
- The cue is layered with at least three distinct audio nodes: a deep impact thump, a descending body sweep and a filtered-noise tail.
- Every frequency endpoint, duration and layer gain is an exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constant (no inline tuning literals in the cue body).
- All cue layers route through the existing master SFX gain so SFX volume/mute apply.
- Unit tests assert layer count, constant-driven amplitude/duration, master routing, the no-AudioContext no-op, and that the cue differs from `playDestructionSound()` and `playPlayerDestructionSound()`.
- `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- Covers parent AC1 and AC5.

# Major-explosion voice limiter

## Goal
Add a concurrency/rate limiter for the major-explosion cue so the per-ship triggers on a wave timeout stay within the GDD §7.3 audio ceiling (no more than 3–4 concurrent SFX instances).

## User story
As a player, a wave-timeout wipe of many ships sounds like one controlled major blast rather than a muddled, clipping pile-up of stacked cues.

## Scope
- Exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` constant (default 4, aligned to the GDD §7.3 "≤ 3–4 concurrent SFX" guidance).
- A voice-cap/rate limiter inside the audio module that counts active major-explosion voices over the cue's longest layer duration.
- Triggers beyond the cap are attenuated/coalesced rather than stacked at full gain; further exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constants control the window and attenuation.
- Limiter state resets on each burst window so later timeouts are not silently dropped.
- Unit tests exercise many simultaneous triggers (e.g. 10 in the same tick).

## Constraints
- Limiter must not affect other cues or the generic/player-destruction paths.
- Must be a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- No gameplay change: pacing/timing of detonations is unchanged.
- The default cap and attenuation are explicitly playtest-tunable (exported constants). [ASSUMPTION: default 4; may be retuned after an audio playtest.]

## Key Files
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — limiter + `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` / window / attenuation constants.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — many-simultaneous-trigger tests.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC (AC3); GDD §7.3 SFX Rate Limiting and §6.7 risk "avoid stacking more than 3–4 concurrent SFX instances".
- Depends on `Major-explosion cue and constants` (the cue must exist first).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` is exported with a default of 4 (within the GDD §7.3 "≤ 3–4 concurrent SFX" ceiling).
- At most `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` major-explosion voices sound concurrently; excess triggers within the active window are attenuated/coalesced rather than stacked at full gain.
- The limiter window/attenuation values are exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constants, and limiter state resets so later timeouts are not silenced.
- Unit tests that fire many simultaneous triggers (e.g. 10 in one tick) assert the active voice count never exceeds the cap and the total gain stays bounded.
- The limiter is a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` and does not alter the generic or player-destruction cues.
- `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- Covers parent AC3.

# Wire major-explosion cue into wave timeout

## Goal
Call `playMajorExplosionSound()` once per detonating non-asteroid survivor in `PlayScene._timeoutWave()`, alongside the existing 10× `destroySelf()` call, while leaving `_loseLife(false)` and its generic life-loss cue untouched.

## User story
As a player, when the level timer hits zero, every surviving enemy that detonates produces the major explosion SFX, so the wipe is heard as a major event.

## Scope
- Import and call `playMajorExplosionSound()` inside the `for (const s of detonateList)` loop in `PlayScene._timeoutWave()`.
- Asteroids (which survive the timeout) must not trigger the cue.
- The no-survivors early return must stay silent (no cue).
- `_loseLife(false)` keeps the generic `playDestructionSound()`; never call `playPlayerDestructionSound()` on this path.
- Tests in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` spy on the cue and assert call counts.

## Constraints
- Feedback only: detonation scale (`WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE`), life penalty and wave advancement are unchanged.
- No new VFX and no gameplay behaviour change.
- The cue is a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (PlayScene tests run headless).

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_timeoutWave()` wiring.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — timeout wiring tests.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC (AC2, AC4); `_timeoutWave()` in `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- Depends on `Major-explosion cue and constants` and `Major-explosion voice limiter`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- In `PlayScene._timeoutWave()`, `playMajorExplosionSound()` is called exactly once per non-asteroid surviving enemy that is detonated, alongside `destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)`.
- A `PlayScene` test spies on the cue and asserts the call count equals the number of detonated survivors, and that asteroids do not trigger it.
- When the timeout fires with no live enemies remaining, no major-explosion cue plays and the wave timer is hidden (existing behaviour unchanged).
- The timeout life-loss path still plays the generic `playDestructionSound()` via `_loseLife(false)` and never `playPlayerDestructionSound()`, verified by tests.
- Detonation scale, one-life penalty and wave advancement are unchanged; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- Covers parent AC2 and AC4.
